title: My Kid's Temperament
description: For a parent to answer about their child (works for toddlers through teens) — discover your child's natural personality style and how to parent it well.

scoring.method: sum points per temperament tag, highest total = child's dominant temperament, second-highest = secondary blend

sanguine.title: Sanguine — "The Spark"
sanguine.inFamily: The loudest laugh in the house, first to make friends at a new school, always narrating their own adventures. Struggles with follow-through, forgets instructions mid-task, and needs a lot of positive attention.
growthEdges: handling correction without taking it personally
parentingTips: Give tasks in small, engaging chunks — long boring stretches lose them fast
Praise generously and specifically; they thrive on positive attention
Redirect rather than lecture — a long talking-to loses them after the first sentence
Channel their energy into performance, sports, or group activities where their spark is an asset

choleric.title: Choleric — "The Little Leader"
choleric.inFamily: Organizes the other kids' games, negotiates bedtime like a lawyer, hates losing at anything. Can be bossy with siblings and push back hard against rules.
growthEdges: softening how they speak to others
parentingTips: Give them real choices where possible — a sense of control reduces power struggles
Explain the "why" behind rules; they respond better to logic than to "because I said so"
Let natural consequences teach where safe to do so, rather than only imposed punishment
Praise their leadership when it's kind, so they learn strength and kindness aren't opposites

melancholic.title: Melancholic — "The Deep Feeler"
melancholic.inFamily: Notices everything, asks big questions, needs real prep time before new situations. Can be a perfectionist about schoolwork or drawings and take teasing hard.
growthEdges: opening up when upset instead of withdrawing
parentingTips: Give advance warning before transitions or new situations — surprises are harder for them
Validate big feelings before problem-solving; they need to feel heard first
Avoid harsh criticism of their work — they're already their own toughest critic
Respect their need for quiet recovery time after a busy or social day

phlegmatic.title: Phlegmatic — "The Steady One"
phlegmatic.inFamily: Easygoing, rarely the source of conflict, content playing quietly for long stretches. Can be slow to try new things and may not speak up about what they actually want.
growthEdges: speaking up for their own preferences
trying new things without a push
not just going along to avoid conflict
parentingTips: Ask directly what they want — they often won't volunteer a preference
Give extra time and gentle encouragement before new activities, rather than rushing them
Don't mistake their quiet for having no opinion; check in one-on-one
Celebrate their steadiness — it's easy to overlook a child who never causes a scene
